elements.element: Vendor duty to defend Customer against third-party claims
elements.evidence: "Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company"

elements.element: Trigger: third-party claim alleging services/deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: "(i) an allegation that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"

elements.element: Trigger: data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: "(iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company's Confidential Information caused by Contractor"

elements.element: Trigger: Vendor gross negligence or wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "(iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct"
"Company shall give Contractor prompt written notice of any such claim"
"Contractor shall have sole control of the defense and settlement"

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: No Customer indemnity exists in the clause or document; conditional requirement is demonstrably absent
"an allegation that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"
No exclusions appear; clause is limited only by "to the extent arising out of"
No infringement remedy mechanic is inserted

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3x annual fees
elements.evidence: "are not subject to the limitations set forth in Sections 7(a), 7(b) and 7(c)" — uncapped, no 3x cap

offending_extra_words: provided that no settlement imposing any liability or admission on Company shall be made without Company's prior written consent
reasons: All atomic elements of the preferred position are met: defence and indemnity for Company and affiliates, all four triggers (IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), and notice/control/cooperation mechanics; the Customer-indemnity limitation is conditional and the condition is absent because no Customer indemnity exists.
Minimality fails: 'hold harmless' adds protection beyond the preferred prose's defend-and-indemnify formulation.
Minimality fails: the settlement-consent proviso is a mechanic beyond the preferred notice, control and cooperation set.

Minimality fails: the heading was rewritten by a replace operation ('INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR' to 'INDEMNIFICATION') when a concise insert_after of the new subsection alone would suffice for an absent clause.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no exclusions, no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, no 3x annual fees super-cap), but that is immaterial since the locked target is preferred.

Intent is preserved: subsections (a)-(c) remain effective and the carve-out references existing sections; note 'Works' should be confirmed as a defined term elsewhere in the Agreement to avoid a dangling reference.
